Against it: only four language definitions were ever built (Java, JavaScript, Python, TypeScript — none for Rust or Go), the TypeScript definition alone is 6,297 lines of a bespoke `.tsg` DSL, resolution is a binary path-exists/doesn't search with no precision-tier concept, and GitHub archived the entire repo in September 2025 with no successor ("if you wish to continue development, fork it"). Production usage was real while it lasted (GitHub's own Precise Code Navigation, Python Dec 2021 / TypeScript Mar 2024). Verdict: skip: see §5.
docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md:76:**difftastic** ([Wilfred/difftastic](https://github.com/Wilfred/difftastic)). Confirmed from the author's own writeup ("Difftastic, the Fantastic Diff") that diffing is framed as shortest-path search (Dijkstra) over a DAG of `(left_position, right_position, parent-exit-stack)` vertices built from a uniform s-expression form of each tree-sitter tree — a sequential positional alignment, not general tree-edit-distance over subtree identity. A follow-up optimization writeup ("How do I boost difftastic by 4x") shows the real engineering cost is almost entirely vertex-memory-layout work (shrinking the `Vertex` struct, pruning zero-weight-edge chains, allocator choice), not algorithm choice — A* was tried and dropped for no real improvement over Dijkstra. Move detection is explicitly unimplemented: Wilfred's own issue #508 (opened 2023) proposes it as future work and it remains open. Adding a language needs a tree-sitter grammar plus `atom_nodes` (which node kinds are leaves despite having children) and `delimiter_tokens` (paired delimiters) — real per-language tuning, misconfiguring either produces spurious diffs. Verdict: the core algorithm is overkill for monokl's actual need (semantic "what changed," not minimal general-purpose text diff); see §2/§5 for what's still worth borrowing (uniform IR, per-language leaf/delimiter config, and beating difftastic on move detection specifically since it still doesn't have any).
docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md:128:Triggered by two things landing together: real usage-ranking data (GitHub Octoverse 2025, TIOBE July 2026, Stack Overflow 2025) showing C (TIOBE #2) and C++ (TIOBE #3) both ranked above Java and completely absent from this roadmap, and a question raised back in §6 by studying codegraph but never resolved — whether monokl should add a generic, thinly-configured tree-sitter tier for languages that don't merit Go/Java-level hand-tuned investment. Kotlin and Swift (real candidates for Android/mobile reach) were evaluated as part of the same pass.
docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md:132:**The premise this idea was sold on doesn't survive contact with the evidence, and the design has to account for that rather than assume it away.** codegraph — the tool whose 30+-language reach originally motivated this — does not actually keep its per-language config thin in production. Its own architecture docs and issue tracker show real, sustained special-casing: Kotlin needs custom nested-property-declaration visiting, Java needs Lombok-generated-member synthesis (the exact problem this spec already solved bespoke for `lang-java`), C# needs generic-unwrapping and nullable-stripping, C++ needs smart-pointer unwrapping, COBOL needs a fixed-to-free preprocessing pass before parsing even starts — and codegraph's maintainers describe this as ongoing, expected growth, not a one-time cost that levels off. "Thin config" is this idea's aspiration, not a description of what shipped multi-language tooling actually requires once real usage arrives. Consequence: any fallback-tier language that gets real traction will generate the same pressure, and it has to be actively capped by policy — the `Heuristic`/`Structural` ceiling and the no-`InspectEntry` rule above are that cap, not a suggestion to relax once a language proves popular. A language that needs more than that cap allows is a graduation candidate (see below), not a reason to widen the fallback tier's own scope.
docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md:134:Real precedent for the _shape_ itself, independent of codegraph's specific execution: universal- ctags already runs a structurally similar two-tier model — hand-written full parsers for complex languages, plus a genuinely generic, user-extensible regex-based "optlib" mechanism for everything else, which validates `Heuristic`-only as the honest ceiling for a truly thin tier rather than something to reach past. More importantly, Sourcegraph ships close to this exact shape in production today: fast, always-available search-based navigation (generically powered by ctags and tree-sitter) as a fallback alongside precise SCIP/LSIF navigation for repos with a real indexer — credible evidence this two-tier product shape is genuinely load-bearing, not a compromise nobody actually uses. (GitHub Linguist was checked and is _not_ real precedent here — it's heuristic pattern-matching for language identification, not AST-based code intelligence, and doesn't validate this specific tier.)
docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md:146:- **Scala** — official grammar is stale (a year old) and explicitly does not support Scala 3 syntax, now the dialect most real Scala code is written in. Shipping it would mean silently misparsing the modern language, not a coverage gap that degrades gracefully. **§12 has a real answer for Scala too**, and a stronger one than Kotlin's: Scalameta, a mature JVM-subprocess parser with Scala 3 support solved since 2021-22 and a direct precedent for monokl's exact use case (`scalex`, "Scala code intelligence for coding agents. Zero Build Server. Zero Compilation.").
docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md:177:The compilation-database problem (real semantic analysis needs real include paths and macros, normally from `compile_commands.json`) degrades gracefully rather than failing outright — clangd's own docs confirm it falls back to generic default flags and a documented degraded mode when no compilation database exists. More useful: **`-frecovery-ast`** (RecoveryExpr) has been on by default in Clang since version 11 (2020) specifically so clangd keeps working on broken/WIP code — it preserves AST nodes across semantic errors (unresolved identifiers, overload failures, missing members). This is Clang's own team already solving, at the semantic layer, the exact "tolerate broken code" problem tree-sitter structurally cannot touch since it has no semantic layer at all. The win is bounded, though: RecoveryExpr only helps once a file is found and parsed — a missing `#include` is a preprocessor-level fatal error with no equivalent recovery flag, a real and frequently-reported complaint (clangd#695 and others). So Clang clears `Heuristic` easily for self-contained or system-header-only files; for header-heavy real-world C++ lacking real include paths, it's back near tree-sitter's ceiling.
docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md:193:The open daemon/session-mode question (§4) got a dedicated, research-backed design pass: a 16-agent workflow (9 per-language backend studies — TypeScript, Rust, Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, Scala, C/C++, and a combined C#/Ruby/PHP pass — 3 cross-cutting architecture questions, 3 adversarial critiques of a draft design, and one synthesis) stress-tested a proposed `PrecisionUpgrader` trait against how real semantic backends for every language on this roadmap actually behave, rather than designing it in the abstract. The result is substantial enough to need its own file rather than another entry here, per this log's own convention for substantial changes: see **[06-daemon-architecture.md](./06-daemon-architecture.md)** for the full design — the trait shape, the lifetime model (and why it needs to nest and distinguish owned-vs-attached), the `DaemonExtension` ingestion model, a `PrecisionLedger` for attaching confidence after the fact (eagerly, lazily, or retroactively, decoupled from `FileAnalysis`'s own cache lifecycle), confidence-signaling rules, and the per-language lifetime table.
docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md:195:Headline result, in brief: the core shape survived (every backend maps onto `PerCall`/ `PerInvocation`/`Session` as a real cost ceiling, no language demanded a fourth tier), but the trait's _return type_ did not — five independent per-language studies (Kotlin, Go, Scala, Rust, C++) converged on the same finding that "promote a bare `CapabilityPrecision`" destroys real candidate sets, dual precision axes, and structured facts the underlying tools actually hand back. Also produced: real backend identification per language (`typescript-go`/TS 7.0's new LSP server went GA July 8, 2026, superseding the plain-tsserver assumption; Python's `Pyrefly`/`ty` are genuinely Rust-implemented but still subprocess/LSP-integrated, not embeddable libraries; Java's `jdtls` import step hard-crashes via OOM past ~3000 files, a real gate requirement, not a graceful degradation; Kotlin's `kotlin-lsp` is real but still built on the same unstable-per-JetBrains foundation already flagged, just hidden behind a heavier IDE-embedding shell); and a confirmed, structural gap in both LSP and SCIP — neither protocol carries a confidence field, so the compilers' own internal degradation signals (Clang's `RecoveryExpr`, JDT's `isRecovered()`) have to be recovered via a per-backend sentinel table, not trusted from protocol silence.
docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md:208:- **No cancellation** — rust-analyzer cancels because Salsa's memo table is shared mutable storage and a write waits for readers to die (`docs/book/src/contributing/architecture.md`; `ty`'s `trigger_cancellation` in `crates/ty_project/src/db.rs`). Monokl's index is immutable after build; `apply_change` swaps an `Arc`, old snapshots go stale, `Snapshot::is_current` says so. Removes `Cancellable<T>`, `catch_unwind`, and `UnwindSafe` bounds from the API.
docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md:215:- **`Snapshot::query(&QueryRequest) -> QueryResponse`** with index-parallel `Vec<OpOutcome>` (DataLoader's ordering contract), one `BudgetReport`, one `Provenance`, `Detail::{Lite, Full}` degrade-before-drop (LSP 3.17 `workspaceSymbol/resolve`), and a `deadline`. Justification is intermediate results never entering model context (Anthropic, *code execution with MCP*: 150k → 2k tokens) and snapshot atomicity, not the shared budget. Neither LSP (Base Protocol 0.9 line 122) nor MCP (2025-11-25 tools spec) batches at the protocol level, so batching can only live inside one call.
docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md:217:- **`SymbolId` SCIP-compatible at the string, not the container**; no path, no kind, no line in identity; `Local` derived from scope structure rather than SCIP's per-document counter — `scip.proto` lines 157–179, `docs/DESIGN.md` ("not meant as a storage format for querying"), rust-analyzer `cli/scip.rs` (`local_count` reset per document; four `FIXME` tests for nested items).
docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md:240:- **The budget seam: core measures, the caller budgets** (Part 8 §7.3–§7.5, §9.1). Part 8 put `budget: Budget` and `policy: BudgetPolicy` on `monokl-core`'s `QueryRequest` while §9.1 put `Budget`, `BudgetPolicy`, `apply_budget`, and tiktoken in `monokl-agent`, and §7.2's own flow diagram labelled `apply_budget` a `monokl-agent` step inside `Snapshot::query` — a `monokl-core` method. Resolved by taking §9.1 literally: core returns fully ranked, uncapped results plus `cost: Vec<OpCost>` under a `Limits` memory ceiling, and every budget is allocated one layer up by two peer allocators, `monokl-agent` for the CLI and Wisp's `wisp-context` for a briefing. Three alternatives were rejected on evidence: a caller-supplied `measure` closure has no digest and so breaks `OperationId::normalized_params` and `provenance_is_current`; a fixed tokens-per-byte constant is either a 3.8x overrun risk (measured 3.78 bytes/token on Rust source, adversarial worst case 1.0) or the byte bound with extra ceremony; and a core-side token budget forces the caller to guess a code sub-budget before knowing what its other sections cost, reintroducing the round trip §7.1 cites Anthropic's *code execution with MCP* result to eliminate. `SkipReason::BudgetExhausted` is deleted; `SkipReason` and `Detail` are otherwise unchanged, and `Detail` gains the acceptance criterion `lite(full(x)) == lite_direct(x)` without which caller-side degrade is unsound.
docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md:267:Four correction families from that pass are applied directly to the reconstruction source. Part 2 now distinguishes structural/textual captures from semantic resolution; the planned `oxc_semantic` pass remains gated on an owned range/binding record that survives the arena and composes with cross-file dependency resolution. Parts 1 and 3 replace `Option<resolved path>` with typed resolved/ambiguous/unresolved/external dependency outcomes, use a validated non-empty/sorted/deduplicated ambiguity wrapper, classify successfully resolved out-of-workspace targets as external, and define resolver/query behavior for each. Part 6 replaces static provenance labels with runtime analyzer and operation identities, adds typed backend-decline reasons, and specifies a bounded, degradable LSP lifecycle. Part 8 pins each snapshot's analyses inside its immutable index—rather than exposing the mutable path-keyed cache—then makes query-visible failed-change publication and incremental-versus-clean equivalence explicit. These refinements were required because the first draft's public `Vec` could deserialize an invalid ambiguity, its TS resolver conflated out-of-scope success with in-workspace resolution, and its old snapshot could otherwise observe a new cache value before index publication.
docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md:269:The comparison does **not** reopen rejected architecture. Atlas's persistent SQLite/FTS store is useful precedent for complete publication, not a reason to add a persistent search index. Serena supplies lifecycle fixtures, not a Python dependency. `sem-core` is a dev-only differential oracle candidate, not a second production analysis stack. Repowise's compiler-oracle methodology is adopted for facts Monokl actually owns; its call-graph product surface is not. OpenWiki overlaps Wisp's grounded documentation lifecycle more than Monokl's analyzer core.
docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md:308:- **TypeScript analyzer, part 1.** The nesting-depth guard is 256, not caliper's 2000: a 2000-deep file overflowed a 2 MiB thread stack, and a stack overflow aborts the process, so `catch_unwind` cannot save it. A too-deep file, a fatal parse error and a contained panic all return the same degraded analysis (`had_parse_errors`, empty extraction). `resolved_import_graph` is `Unsupported` and `classified_imports` false until resolution lands, instead of Part 3's values. Departures from Section 17: a default import's `imported` is `"default"`; a function's signature is the text up to its body, not to the first `{`; `.js` files parse with JSX; and the export code follows OXC 0.151's split `ExportDeclaration`/`ExportNamedDeclaration`/`ExportFromDeclaration` AST.

Ratified by the owner 2026-10-23.

- **Part 8 over Part 1.** Where Part 1's v0.1.0 text and Part 8 conflict, Part 8 governs core: results are fully ranked, deduped and uncapped, with counts; no tiktoken, budget or caps in core; core result types such as `FileAnalysis` are not `Serialize`; `.monokl/cache.json` gets its own `persist::v1` types. Rejected: porting Part 1 as written, which keeps one type set serving the Rust API, the cache format and the wire shape, three compatibility clocks on one struct. Tracks still to be specced (12, 14, 16–22) are drafted against Part 8; Part 1 remains the reconstruction source where Part 8 is silent.
- **One crate.** The core/agent boundary is two modules in `crates/monokl` with an architecture test, not two crates (ADR 0003). Rejected: splitting now, which buys a compiler-enforced boundary at the cost of a second crate before anything outside monokl consumes core.

## 20. Analyzer foundation corrections (2026-10-23)

- **`Ord` on `LanguageId`.** Part 3 §11 keeps a `BTreeSet<LanguageId>` to deduplicate skip diagnostics, but Part 1 §11 derives no `PartialOrd`/`Ord`, so the spec does not compile. `LanguageId` derives both, in declaration order. Rejected: a hash set in Part 3, since both Part 3 and the contract doc name a sorted set.
- **Other departures from Part 1.** `AnalyzerCapabilities` also derives `PartialEq`/`Eq` so analyzers can be tested against expected values. `FileAnalysis` takes `digest: Digest` for `content_hash` (SPEC-011) and records the `profile` it was built under (owner decision: fixed fields per profile, recorded, so the cache never serves a `Dependencies` result as `Full`). `language()` keeps Part 1's `&str`.
- **For later tracks.** What an analyzer does when `analyze_with_profile` gets a path `supports` rejects is left to the registry track, which checks `supports` first. Part 3's `language_label` matches only 5 of the 13 `LanguageId` variants and will not compile as written.

## 21. Phase 1: a runnable `monokl search` (2026-10-24)

Decisions made while building the first end-to-end command, with the departures from Parts 1 and 3 they required.

- **#21, query with only excluded terms.** Returns an empty result with one `Skipped` diagnostic ("query has no positive terms"). Empty and operator-only queries stay silent. Rejected: silent empty, which looks like "matched nothing".
- **BM25 terms.** Each non-excluded literal term goes through `tokens::tokenize`, deduplicated, in query order; regex terms add matched lines and keywords but no BM25 terms. One case-insensitive, fail-fast regex engine serves text search and per-term matching, so the two stages cannot disagree (§18 #7). The excluded-terms pass searches with no file ceiling so a file past the ceiling still excludes.
- **Budget (agent layer).** Defaults 50 results / 20,000 tokens / 2 MiB. Blocks over 32 KiB are counted by byte length, an upper bound, instead of tokenized, so `total_tokens` can overcount for them. The cut is a prefix in rank order: a first block larger than the budget leaves an empty, truncated result. The marker is michi's `TruncationOutcome` hint.
- **TypeScript analyzer, part 1.** The nesting-depth guard is 256, not caliper's 2000: a 2000-deep file overflowed a 2 MiB thread stack, and a stack overflow aborts the process, so `catch_unwind` cannot save it. A too-deep file, a fatal parse error and a contained panic all return the same degraded analysis (`had_parse_errors`, empty extraction). `resolved_import_graph` is `Unsupported` and `classified_imports` false until resolution lands, instead of Part 3's values. Departures from Section 17: a default import's `imported` is `"default"`; a function's signature is the text up to its body, not to the first `{`; `.js` files parse with JSX; and the export code follows OXC 0.151's split `ExportDeclaration`/`ExportNamedDeclaration`/`ExportFromDeclaration` AST.
- **CLI.** Results print on stdout; errors are structured michi errors on stderr with exit 1; usage errors exit 2. Paths print relative to the working directory when under it. Reaching the file ceiling adds a `Warning` diagnostic.
- **Property tests.** Reference-implementation properties for ranking, dedup, tokenizing and the query parser found no bugs. `#[non_exhaustive]` is on the enums that will grow and on `TextSearchResult`; `Digest`, `CapabilityPrecision`, option structs and `Modifier` are left exact on purpose.
- **Still open.** `+regex:`/`-regex:` lose their modifier (#8), and there is no per-term length cap (#16).

name: rust-style
description: Apply when writing or modifying Rust code in this project.
---

**Goal:** Code correct by construction, readable under churn, performant in hot paths.

## Project-specific decisions

These are non-negotiables, not preferences:

- Internal maps: `FxHashMap`. JSON-output maps: `BTreeMap` (deterministic key ordering).
- Paths: `camino::Utf8Path`/`Utf8PathBuf`, not `std::path`, unless the path is by definition not UTF-8.
- No `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` — use `?` and let callers decide what to do with failure.

## Control flow

`let...else` keeps the happy path flat:

```rust
let Some(entry) = map.get(key) else { return None };
let Ok(parsed) = input.parse::<u32>() else { continue };
```

## Matching

No wildcards — a compile error on unhandled variants is a feature:

```rust
match status { Status::Ok => .., Status::Err => .. }  // compiler tells you when Status grows
match status { Status::Ok => .., _ => .. }             // silently misses new variants
```

Full `match` over `matches!` for the same reason.

## Types

Newtypes when a bare type allows confusion. Enums when a bool parameter hides intent:

```rust
struct ContentHash([u8; 32]);             // not: [u8; 32]
enum Visibility { Public, Private }      // not: is_public: bool
```

Explicit destructuring gets compiler errors when structs change:

```rust
let SymbolEntry { name, kind, .. } = entry;
```

## Naming

Shadow variables through transformations — no `raw_`/`parsed_`/`trimmed_` prefixes:

```rust
let path = args.path;
let path = path.canonicalize()?;
let path = path.join("config.toml");
```

## Comments

Only when the WHY is non-obvious: a hidden constraint, a workaround, a non-obvious invariant. Not what the code does.
118:- `Arc<dyn LanguageAnalyzer>` throughout so the registry is thread-shareable across rayon workers.

#!/bin/bash
# Usage: bisect.sh <binary> <mode> <stack_kib> <shape...>
# Prints the largest depth that does not overflow and the implied stack bytes per level.
bin="$1"; mode="$2"; stack="$3"; shift 3
for shape in "$@"; do
  lo=0; hi=400000
  if "$bin" "$mode" "$shape" "$hi" "$stack" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "$shape $mode: no overflow at $hi"
    continue
  fi
  while [ $((hi - lo)) -gt $((hi / 100 + 1)) ]; do
    mid=$(((lo + hi) / 2))
    if "$bin" "$mode" "$shape" "$mid" "$stack" >/dev/null 2>&1; then lo=$mid; else hi=$mid; fi
  done
  echo "$shape $mode: max_ok=$lo bytes_per_level=$((stack * 1024 / (lo > 0 ? lo : 1)))"
done

53-# Version catalogue. A crate adds an entry to its own [dependencies] only when code uses it.
54-[workspace.dependencies]
# List available commands
default:
    @just --list

# Install the cargo tools the recipes below use
install-tools:
    cargo install cargo-nextest cargo-llvm-cov cargo-machete cargo-mutants cargo-deny typos-cli zizmor --locked
    rustup component add llvm-tools-preview

# Install the pinned toolchain and the moon-managed git hooks
setup:
    proto install
    moon sync vcs-hooks

# Build the workspace. One `cargo --workspace` invocation, not `moon run :build`: per-crate cargo processes all
# contend for the same target/ lock and serialize.
build:
    cargo build --workspace --locked

build-release:
    cargo build --workspace --release --locked

# Run tests with nextest, plus doctests, which nextest does not run. The default-features pass catches code that only
# builds because --all-features turned something on.
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --locked
    cargo nextest run --workspace --locked
    cargo test --doc --workspace --all-features --locked

# Line coverage; with a threshold, fails below it
coverage threshold="":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --locked --lcov --output-path lcov.info
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only
    if [[ -n "{{ threshold }}" ]]; then
      cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{ threshold }}"
    fi

# Coverage report, opened in the browser
coverage-html:
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --locked --html --open

# Format check and clippy, with and without default features
lint:
    cargo fmt --all --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --no-default-features --locked -- -D warnings

# Clippy on the crates moon reports as affected, in one cargo invocation
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then exit 0; fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings

fmt:
    cargo fmt --all

# Documentation build, with warnings (including broken intra-doc links) as errors
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --all-features --locked
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --locked

# Licenses, advisories, bans and sources
deny:
    cargo deny check

# Unused dependencies
machete:
    cargo machete

typos:
    typos

# Callisto config, package discovery and pending changesets; the same gate as CI's Changesets job
changesets:

input.old_string: _ => panic!("unknown shape {name}"),
input.new_string:
"u_paren" => (format!("const x = {}1", r("(")), "a.ts"),
        "u_bracket" => (format!("const x = {}1", r("[")), "a.ts"),
        "u_block" => (r("{"), "a.ts"),
        "u_tuple" => (format!("type T = {}number", r("[")), "a.ts"),
        "u_ptype" => (format!("type T = {}number", r("(")), "a.ts"),
        "u_tpl" => (format!("const x = {}1", r("`${")), "a.ts"),
        "u_jsx" => (format!("const j = {}", r("<a>")), "a.tsx"),
        "u_jsxexpr" => (format!("const j = <a>{}", r("{<a>")), "a.tsx"),
        "arr_pattern" => (format!("{}a{} = 1;\n", r("["), r("]")), "a.ts"),
        "obj_pattern" => (format!("({}a{} = 1);\n", r("{a:"), r("}")), "a.ts"),
        "arrow_params" => (format!("const f = {}a{} => 1;\n", r("("), r(")")), "a.ts"),
        "arrow_default" => (format!("const f = ({}1) => 1;\n", r("a = (")), "a.ts"),
        "assertion" => (format!("const x = {}1;\n", r("<a>")), "a.ts"),
        "optcall" => (format!("const x = {}1{};\n", r("a?.("), r(")")), "a.ts"),
        "newcall" => (format!("const x = {}1{};\n", r("new A("), r(")")), "a.ts"),
        "computed" => (format!("const x = {}1{};\n", r("{[a]:"), r("}")), "a.ts"),

content.content:
1	# Language Analyzer Contract — Semantic Model
2	
3	Source: `docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md` §11 (`analysis/lang.rs` — `LanguageAnalyzer` trait
4	verbatim, lines ~1290-1381); `docs/spec/03-multi-language-platform.md` §3 (`analysis/registry.rs`
5	— `AnalyzerRegistry`, lines ~219-291) and §11 (capability-driven query gating,
6	`require_precision_capability`/`add_missing_analyzer_diagnostic`, lines ~1780-1990).
7	Cross-referenced against `docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md` Part 3 findings #6, #10, #14.
8	
9	No crate exists yet — code blocks below are spec-verbatim Rust, not source files. Treat this doc
10	as authoritative until code exists, then re-point at source paths.
11	
12	## `LanguageAnalyzer` trait (`analysis/lang.rs`)
13	
14	The most load-bearing contract in the crate — `AnalyzerRegistry`, capability gating, and every
15	command's diagnostic behavior are built on top of it.
16	
17	```rust
18	pub trait LanguageAnalyzer: Send + Sync {
19	    fn languages(&self) -> &[LanguageId];
20	    fn supports(&self, path: &Utf8Path) -> bool;
21	    fn language_for(&self, path: &Utf8Path) -> Option<LanguageId>;
22	    fn capabilities(&self, language: LanguageId) -> AnalyzerCapabilities;
23	
24	    fn analyze_with_profile(
25	        &self,
26	        path: &Utf8Path,
27	        source: Box<dyn FnOnce() -> Result<String>>,
28	        profile: AnalysisProfile,
29	    ) -> Result<Arc<FileAnalysis>>;
30	
31	    /// Full-fidelity convenience wrapper — the only profile v0.1.0 code ever requests.
32	    fn analyze(&self, path: &Utf8Path, source: Box<dyn FnOnce() -> Result<String>>) -> Result<Arc<FileAnalysis>> {
33	        self.analyze_with_profile(path, source, AnalysisProfile::Full)
34	    }
35	}
36	```
37	
38	### Signature fix — must not regress to single-language shape (invariant)
39	
40	§11 carries a "Post-research correction" note: an earlier draft declared only `supports`/`analyze`,
41	leaving Part 3's `AnalyzerRegistry` calling `language_id()`/`capabilities()`/`analyze_with_profile()`
42	that didn't exist on the trait — a compile-breaking gap caught in a post-hoc audit. Corrected shape:
43	
44	1. **`languages(&self) -> &[LanguageId]`** — a slice, not a zero-arg `language_id() -> LanguageId`.
45	   One analyzer instance can own several languages: `TsAnalyzer`/`RustAnalyzer` return a
46	   one-element slice; the generic tree-sitter fallback tier (05-research-and-decisions.md §10)
47	   returns several (C, Cpp, Bash, CSharp, Ruby, Php, Kotlin, Scala).
48	2. **`language_for(&self, path) -> Option<LanguageId>`** — new method, absent from the broken
49	   draft. Which specific language among `languages()` a path maps to; `None` only if `supports`
50	   would also be `false`. Single-language analyzers: `supports(path).then_some(<their one id>)`.
51	   Fallback tier: its own extension table.
52	3. **`capabilities(&self, language) -> AnalyzerCapabilities`** — parameterized, not zero-arg.
53	   Necessary because one fallback-tier instance has different precision ceilings per language
54	   (C reaches `Structural`, C++ stays `Heuristic` pending the optional Clang tier, §12).
55	
56	**Do not collapse back to one-analyzer-one-language.** That shape can't express the fallback tier
57	and is the exact defect the correction fixed — any impl reverting to it is implementing the wrong
58	contract.
59	
60	## `AnalysisProfile` / `CapabilityPrecision`
61	
62	```rust
63	pub enum AnalysisProfile { Dependencies, Structural, Full }
64	// Dependencies: skips symbol/export/block extraction. Structural: skips inspect-entry pass.
65	// Full: everything, including per-language InspectEntry classification.
66	
67	#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
68	pub enum CapabilityPrecision { Unsupported, Heuristic, Structural, Exact }
69	```
70	
71	`Ord` derived in this order — gating code compares with `<` (`precision < CapabilityPrecision::Structural`), not just `==`.
72	
73	- `Unsupported` — can't answer this surface at all for this language.
74	- `Heuristic` — regex/extension-based, no real parse (Rust's fallback when `lang-rs` off; the
75	  tree-sitter fallback tier for most languages).
76	- `Structural` — real AST parse, approximate resolution — e.g. Rust's `use` heuristic, which can't
77	  distinguish a submodule from an external crate without crate-graph resolution.
78	- `Exact` — real resolution. Only `TsAnalyzer.resolved_import_graph` reaches this (via
79	  `oxc_resolver`); TS's own `refs`/`definition`/`inspect_detail` are `Structural`, not `Exact`.
80	
81	## `AnalyzerCapabilities`
82	
83	```rust
84	pub struct AnalyzerCapabilities {
85	    pub blocks: bool,
86	    pub classified_imports: bool,
87	    pub resolved_import_graph: CapabilityPrecision,
88	    pub refs: CapabilityPrecision,
89	    pub definition: CapabilityPrecision,
90	    pub inspect_detail: CapabilityPrecision,
91	}
92	```
93	
94	Per-language, not per-analyzer — callers must only pass a `language` value this analyzer's own
95	`languages()`/`language_for()` actually returned.
96	
97	## `AnalyzerRegistry` (`analysis/registry.rs`)
98	
99	```rust
100	pub struct AnalyzerRegistry { analyzers: Vec<Arc<dyn LanguageAnalyzer>>, config_hash: String }
101	
102	impl AnalyzerRegistry {
103	    pub fn analyzer_for(&self, path: &Utf8Path) -> Option<&dyn LanguageAnalyzer> {
104	        self.analyzers.iter().find(|a| a.supports(path)).map(Arc::as_ref)
105	    }
106	    pub fn supports_language(&self, path: &Utf8Path, languages: &[LanguageId]) -> bool {
107	        self.analyzer_for(path).and_then(|a| a.language_for(path)).is_some_and(|l| languages.contains(&l))
108	    }
109	}
110	```
111	
112	- **First-match-by-registration-order, not specificity** — linear `find`, first `supports(path)`
113	  wins. TS registers first when `lang-ts` is enabled, Rust always after.
114	- `config_hash` = each analyzer's own hash joined with `::` (`TsAnalyzer::config_hash_for(opts)` +
115	  literal `"rust-analyzer-v1"`) — feeds `analysis::persist::init`'s cache key.
116	- **No match → `None`, no diagnostic from the registry itself.** Caller's job — see
117	  `add_missing_analyzer_diagnostic` below, which has its own gap (#10).
118	- `Arc<dyn LanguageAnalyzer>` throughout so the registry is thread-shareable across rayon workers.
119	
120	## Capability-driven query gating
121	
122	`require_precision_capability` (03-multi-language-platform.md §11) is the single decision point
123	every gated command (`search`, `inspect`, `dependents`, `refs`, `definition`) calls through — no

# Language Analyzer Contract — Semantic Model

Source: `docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md` §11 (`analysis/lang.rs` — `LanguageAnalyzer` trait
verbatim, lines ~1290-1381); `docs/spec/03-multi-language-platform.md` §3 (`analysis/registry.rs`
— `AnalyzerRegistry`, lines ~219-291) and §11 (capability-driven query gating,
`require_precision_capability`/`add_missing_analyzer_diagnostic`, lines ~1780-1990).
Cross-referenced against `docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md` Part 3 findings #6, #10, #14.

No crate exists yet — code blocks below are spec-verbatim Rust, not source files. Treat this doc
as authoritative until code exists, then re-point at source paths.

## `LanguageAnalyzer` trait (`analysis/lang.rs`)

The most load-bearing contract in the crate — `AnalyzerRegistry`, capability gating, and every
command's diagnostic behavior are built on top of it.

```rust
pub trait LanguageAnalyzer: Send + Sync {
    fn languages(&self) -> &[LanguageId];
    fn supports(&self, path: &Utf8Path) -> bool;
    fn language_for(&self, path: &Utf8Path) -> Option<LanguageId>;
    fn capabilities(&self, language: LanguageId) -> AnalyzerCapabilities;

    fn analyze_with_profile(
        &self,
        path: &Utf8Path,
        source: Box<dyn FnOnce() -> Result<String>>,
        profile: AnalysisProfile,
    ) -> Result<Arc<FileAnalysis>>;

    /// Full-fidelity convenience wrapper — the only profile v0.1.0 code ever requests.
    fn analyze(&self, path: &Utf8Path, source: Box<dyn FnOnce() -> Result<String>>) -> Result<Arc<FileAnalysis>> {
        self.analyze_with_profile(path, source, AnalysisProfile::Full)
    }
}
```

### Signature fix — must not regress to single-language shape (invariant)

§11 carries a "Post-research correction" note: an earlier draft declared only `supports`/`analyze`,
leaving Part 3's `AnalyzerRegistry` calling `language_id()`/`capabilities()`/`analyze_with_profile()`
that didn't exist on the trait — a compile-breaking gap caught in a post-hoc audit. Corrected shape:

1. **`languages(&self) -> &[LanguageId]`** — a slice, not a zero-arg `language_id() -> LanguageId`.
   One analyzer instance can own several languages: `TsAnalyzer`/`RustAnalyzer` return a
   one-element slice; the generic tree-sitter fallback tier (05-research-and-decisions.md §10)
   returns several (C, Cpp, Bash, CSharp, Ruby, Php, Kotlin, Scala).
2. **`language_for(&self, path) -> Option<LanguageId>`** — new method, absent from the broken
   draft. Which specific language among `languages()` a path maps to; `None` only if `supports`
   would also be `false`. Single-language analyzers: `supports(path).then_some(<their one id>)`.
   Fallback tier: its own extension table.
3. **`capabilities(&self, language) -> AnalyzerCapabilities`** — parameterized, not zero-arg.
   Necessary because one fallback-tier instance has different precision ceilings per language
   (C reaches `Structural`, C++ stays `Heuristic` pending the optional Clang tier, §12).

**Do not collapse back to one-analyzer-one-language.** That shape can't express the fallback tier
and is the exact defect the correction fixed — any impl reverting to it is implementing the wrong
contract.

## `AnalysisProfile` / `CapabilityPrecision`

```rust
pub enum AnalysisProfile { Dependencies, Structural, Full }
// Dependencies: skips symbol/export/block extraction. Structural: skips inspect-entry pass.
// Full: everything, including per-language InspectEntry classification.

#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub enum CapabilityPrecision { Unsupported, Heuristic, Structural, Exact }
```

`Ord` derived in this order — gating code compares with `<` (`precision < CapabilityPrecision::Structural`), not just `==`.

- `Unsupported` — can't answer this surface at all for this language.
- `Heuristic` — regex/extension-based, no real parse (Rust's fallback when `lang-rs` off; the
  tree-sitter fallback tier for most languages).
- `Structural` — real AST parse, approximate resolution — e.g. Rust's `use` heuristic, which can't
  distinguish a submodule from an external crate without crate-graph resolution.
- `Exact` — real resolution. Only `TsAnalyzer.resolved_import_graph` reaches this (via
  `oxc_resolver`); TS's own `refs`/`definition`/`inspect_detail` are `Structural`, not `Exact`.

## `AnalyzerCapabilities`

```rust
pub struct AnalyzerCapabilities {
    pub blocks: bool,
    pub classified_imports: bool,
    pub resolved_import_graph: CapabilityPrecision,
    pub refs: CapabilityPrecision,
    pub definition: CapabilityPrecision,
    pub inspect_detail: CapabilityPrecision,
}
```

Per-language, not per-analyzer — callers must only pass a `language` value this analyzer's own
`languages()`/`language_for()` actually returned.

## `AnalyzerRegistry` (`analysis/registry.rs`)

```rust
pub struct AnalyzerRegistry { analyzers: Vec<Arc<dyn LanguageAnalyzer>>, config_hash: String }

impl AnalyzerRegistry {
    pub fn analyzer_for(&self, path: &Utf8Path) -> Option<&dyn LanguageAnalyzer> {
        self.analyzers.iter().find(|a| a.supports(path)).map(Arc::as_ref)
    }
    pub fn supports_language(&self, path: &Utf8Path, languages: &[LanguageId]) -> bool {
        self.analyzer_for(path).and_then(|a| a.language_for(path)).is_some_and(|l| languages.contains(&l))
    }
}
```

- **First-match-by-registration-order, not specificity** — linear `find`, first `supports(path)`
  wins. TS registers first when `lang-ts` is enabled, Rust always after.
- `config_hash` = each analyzer's own hash joined with `::` (`TsAnalyzer::config_hash_for(opts)` +
  literal `"rust-analyzer-v1"`) — feeds `analysis::persist::init`'s cache key.
- **No match → `None`, no diagnostic from the registry itself.** Caller's job — see
  `add_missing_analyzer_diagnostic` below, which has its own gap (#10).
- `Arc<dyn LanguageAnalyzer>` throughout so the registry is thread-shareable across rayon workers.

## Capability-driven query gating

`require_precision_capability` (03-multi-language-platform.md §11) is the single decision point
every gated command (`search`, `inspect`, `dependents`, `refs`, `definition`) calls through — no
command hand-rolls a per-language check anymore. Below `requirement.minimum` → `false` (caller
skips) + one `Diagnostic{kind: Skipped}` per language, deduped via `BTreeSet<LanguageId>` (not
per-file). `Structural`-but-not-`Exact` → one `Diagnostic{kind: Warning}` per language, same dedup.
`add_missing_analyzer_diagnostic` is the separate "no analyzer at all" path — see #10.

## Diagnostic-signal gaps — must be resolved, not ported as-is

Open questions for spec@1 (edge-case audit Part 3, findings #6/#10/#14), not resolved designs.

1. **#6 — macro-generated code and inactive `#[cfg(...)]` branches are invisible, zero
   capability/precision signal**, unlike every other Rust precision limitation in the spec. The
   crate-graph heuristic gets a signal (`resolved_import_graph: Structural`); `pick_main_struct`
   — which can arbitrarily pick a platform-dead struct as "the" struct — gets none.
   `AnalyzerCapabilities` has no field for "syntactically present but semantically
   unreachable/unexpanded." Decide: new capability field, or a per-result `Diagnostic` instead of
   a static one. Do not ship `pick_main_struct` silently without picking one.
2. **#10 — the "no analyzer" diagnostic conflates two facts.** `add_missing_analyzer_diagnostic`
   derives its message from `candidate_language(path)`, extension-only (`.ts` → `TypeScript`), and
   doesn't see `TsAnalyzer::supports`'s explicit `.d.ts` exclusion. A `.d.ts` file — TS fully
   supported, this one file intentionally out of scope by design — gets the same
   `"{op} is not supported for TypeScript files in this build"` message a truly-unsupported
   language would get. An agent parsing diagnostics can't tell "no analyzer in this build" from
   "supported language, this file deliberately excluded." Decide: distinguish
   `supports() == false but language recognized`, or add a distinct message template for
   intentional per-file exclusions.
3. **#14 — `Vec<Diagnostic>` has no stated ceiling**, unlike every other result list in the spec
   (symbols: 50/file, 500 total; dependents: 200). Lower priority than #6/#10 — resource-bound
   (pathological workspace → unbounded list), not a correctness/signal gap.

## 21. Phase 1: a runnable `monokl search` (2026-10-24)

Decisions made while building the first end-to-end command, with the departures from Parts 1 and 3 they required.

- **#21, query with only excluded terms.** Returns an empty result with one `Skipped` diagnostic ("query has no positive terms"). Empty and operator-only queries stay silent. Rejected: silent empty, which looks like "matched nothing".
- **BM25 terms.** Each non-excluded literal term goes through `tokens::tokenize`, deduplicated, in query order; regex terms add matched lines and keywords but no BM25 terms. One case-insensitive, fail-fast regex engine serves text search and per-term matching, so the two stages cannot disagree (§18 #7). The excluded-terms pass searches with no file ceiling so a file past the ceiling still excludes.
- **Budget (agent layer).** Defaults 50 results / 20,000 tokens / 2 MiB. Blocks over 32 KiB are counted by byte length, an upper bound, instead of tokenized, so `total_tokens` can overcount for them. The cut is a prefix in rank order: a first block larger than the budget leaves an empty, truncated result. The marker is michi's `TruncationOutcome` hint.
- **TypeScript analyzer, part 1.** The nesting-depth guard is 256, not caliper's 2000: a 2000-deep file overflowed a 2 MiB thread stack, and a stack overflow aborts the process, so `catch_unwind` cannot save it. - **Property tests.** Reference-implementation properties for ranking, dedup, tokenizing and the query parser found no bugs. `#[non_exhaustive]` is on the enums that will grow and on `TextSearchResult`; `Digest`, `CapabilityPrecision`, option structs and `Modifier` are left exact on purpose.
- **Still open.** `+regex:`/`-regex:` lose their modifier (#8), and there is no per-term length cap (#16).

#!/bin/bash
# Runs `monokl search needle .` in each case directory and prints exit code, result header, first row, time and peak RSS.
bin="$1"; root="$2"
for dir in "$root"/*/; do
  name=$(basename "$dir")
  out=$(cd "$dir" && /usr/bin/time -l "$bin" search needle . 2>"$root/$name.time" >"$root/$name.out"; echo $?)
  rss=$(grep "maximum resident set size" "$root/$name.time" | awk '{printf "%.1f MiB", $1/1048576}')
  real=$(grep " real " "$root/$name.time" | awk '{print $1 " s"}')
  abort=$(grep -c "overflowed its stack" "$root/$name.time")
  echo "$name | exit=$out | overflow_msgs=$abort | $real | $rss"
  head -2 "$root/$name.out" | cut -c1-110 | sed 's/^/    /'
done

#!/bin/bash
# Runs `monokl search needle .` in each case directory and prints exit code, result header, first row, time and peak RSS.
bin="$1"; root="$2"
for dir in "$root"/*/; do
  name=$(basename "$dir")
  out=$(cd "$dir" && /usr/bin/time -l "$bin" search needle . 2>"$root/$name.time" >"$root/$name.out"; echo $?)
  rss=$(grep "maximum resident set size" "$root/$name.time" | awk '{printf "%.1f MiB", $1/1048576}')
  real=$(grep " real " "$root/$name.time" | awk '{print $1 " s"}')
  abort=$(grep -c "overflowed its stack" "$root/$name.time")
  echo "$name | exit=$out | overflow_msgs=$abort | $real | $rss"
  head -2 "$root/$name.out" | cut -c1-110 | sed 's/^/    /'
done

content.content:
## Part 1 — `01-core-architecture.md`

### Crash / data-loss / silent-wrong-answer

1. **`dependents` silently drops per-file analysis failures.** `WorkspaceIndex::build`'s rayon closure does `Err(e) => { tracing::warn!(...); None }` on any per-file failure — the file vanishes from the `ImportGraph`/`SymbolIndex` with no diagnostic captured anywhere. Verified correction: `WorkspaceIndex` itself has no `diagnostics` field at all (only `files`, `file_index`, `import_graph`, `symbol_index`), so there's no existing field silently going unpopulated — there's no mechanism at all. `search`/`symbols` surface the same failure class as a structured `Diagnostic` inline during their own per-file analysis; `dependents` routes through `WorkspaceIndex::build` and has nothing comparable to route a dropped-file signal into `DependentsResult.diagnostics`. An agent gets `dependents: []` with no signal the answer might be incomplete.
2. **No panic/stack-overflow guard around the parser.** `parse_full` runs OXC's recursive-descent parser directly inside a `rayon::par_iter()` closure with no `catch_unwind` (unlike the napi FFI boundary, which does wrap for this reason) and no recursion-depth/input-size guard. A genuine stack overflow aborts the process regardless of `catch_unwind`, and the blast radius is the entire in-flight `WorkspaceIndex::build` batch, not just the one bad file.
3. **`FileTooLarge`/`SymlinkRejected` are declared but never enforced in this file's own pipeline.** Part 1's reference `TsAnalyzer::analyze`/`WorkspaceIndex::build` read via plain `std::fs::metadata`/`read_to_string` with no size cap and no symlink check — the doc's own note says enforcement lives in Part 3's `io_safety.rs`, but a reader of Part 1 alone would assume these caps are live in the baseline pipeline.
4. **Concurrent disk-cache writes race with last-writer-wins.** The atomic temp+rename write prevents torn reads/writes but not lost writes: two concurrent `monokl` invocations each load their own cache snapshot and `rename()` over the same path independently — whichever finishes last silently discards the other's newly-cached entries. Self-healing (a lost entry just costs a re-parse), but undocumented.
5. **Corrupted `cache.json` hard-fails instead of self-healing.** `init()` explicitly catches `StaleDiskCache` and rebuilds from empty, but a genuinely malformed JSON (e.g. from a disk-full truncated write, still syntactically "complete" before the paired rename) surfaces as `MonoklError::Json` via `?` and is **not** special-cased — the whole workspace build hard-fails instead of falling back to a cold rebuild the way staleness does.
6. **`StaleDiskCache`'s error message references a CLI subcommand (`mnkl init --rebuild`) that doesn't exist**, and per this file's own `init()` logic, the variant is always intercepted internally and never actually surfaced to a caller — dead code as specified.
7. **Bad `regex:` term: hard error in one search stage, silently dropped in the next.** Stage 4 builds one combined regex from all terms and hard-fails the whole query (`?`) on any invalid pattern; stage 5 builds per-term regexes for highlighting and explicitly "silently drops regex compile failures." Same input problem, two contradictory outcomes within one command.
8. **`+regex:foo` loses more than the comment claims.** The code comment says it "silently loses modifier"; tracing the lexer shows it actually degrades all the way to an optional escaped-literal match on the string `foo` — both the required-modifier *and* the regex semantics are discarded, not just the modifier.
rust-analyzer cancels in-flight queries when a change arrives because Salsa's memo table is mutable storage shared by every outstanding snapshot — a write has to wait for readers to die, so it panics them with a sentinel and catches it at the `ide` boundary. `ty` inherits the same mechanic (`Arc::get_mut` on the database "because `trigger_cancellation` drops all other DB references").

Monokl's `WorkspaceIndex` is never mutated after construction. `apply_change` builds a new `Arc<WorkspaceIndex>` and swaps the pointer. Old snapshots stay internally consistent; they are merely stale, and `Snapshot::is_current` says so in one comparison. Nothing needs to be interrupted.

### 3.1 What this removes

- `Cancellable<T>` from every signature.
- `catch_unwind` from the API boundary.
- `UnwindSafe`/`RefUnwindSafe` bounds from every type.
- The requirement that the host process build with `panic = "unwind"`.

Revisit only if a `PrecisionUpgrader` ([06 §2](./06-daemon-architecture.md)) ever holds a shared mutable backend — and even then, scope cancellation to that upgrader's own `Result`, not the query API.

## 22. A parse cannot overflow its stack (2026-11-02)

Resolves [07](./07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md) Part 1 #2 and replaces §21's reasoning for the nesting guard.

- **What was wrong.** §21 treated the bracket scan as the bound on the parser's recursion. It is not one. A quote inside a regex literal hid the rest of the file from it, and arrow functions, conditionals, generic types and JSX recurse without brackets. In the release CLI, 5,000 parentheses after `/'/`, 20,000 levels of `Array<`, `() =>` or `a ? b :`, or 30,000 nested `<div>` overflowed the 8 MiB main thread and aborted the whole search with no output. OXC 0.152 has no depth limit of its own.
- **Measured** (parse plus extraction, aarch64 macOS, stack per nesting level, optimized / unoptimized): `(` or `[` 1,562 / 3,241 B; `[` in a type 1,701 / 4,581 B, the most per source byte; `{a:` 1,847 / 3,636 B; `Array<` 1,562 / 3,436 B; `() =>` 802 / 965 B; `a ? b :` 704 / 676 B; `<div>` 464 / 1,218 B; `!` 80 / 561 B. Left-deep `a + b` and `a.b()` chains parse in a loop and cost 80 / 561 B per level only in the extractor's visitor.
- **Choice.** Each file is parsed and extracted on its own scoped thread with 8 MiB plus 4 KiB per source byte (12 KiB unoptimized), over twice the worst measured cost per byte. Every recursion level consumes at least one byte, so no input can overflow it. A file needing more than 1 GiB, longer than 254 KiB optimized or 85 KiB unoptimized, is degraded without parsing. A panic or a thread that cannot start also degrades. The 256-deep bracket scan stays as an early exit, now skipping regex literals (told from division by the preceding character) and ending quoted strings at a line break.
- **Cost.** A file under the limit that fools the scan is the worst case: 250,000 unclosed `[` after `return /'/` touches 424 MiB of stack and takes 0.08 s. Of 23,222 local TS/JS source files, 131 (0.56%) exceed 254 KiB, nearly all bundler output. A thread per file moved a whole-repo search from 0.11 s to 0.13 s with identical output.
- **Rejected.** A scan that bounds recursion on its own: telling a regex from a division, or JSX text from code, needs the parser's context, so a crafted file can always desynchronise the scan, and then nothing bounds the stack. A fixed large stack with the scan as the bound has the same hole. A child process per file survives any overflow but costs a spawn per file and is not available to library callers. `stacker` cannot reach OXC's recursion. A stack proportional to length with no limit lets a 5 MB file reserve 20 GiB and touch 8 GiB.

README.md:24:- **Output sized for an agent's context.** Results are a compact table with paths relative to where you ran it, capped at 50 results, 20,000 tokens and 2 MiB by default. When something is cut, the output says how many more matched and suggests narrowing the query.

docs/spec/06-daemon-architecture.md:118:**Lifetimes nest.** rust-analyzer's own `proc-macro-srv-cli` is a subprocess loaded once and reused for many expansions with crash-supervision — living inside an otherwise-`PerInvocation` Salsa database build. A flat `lifetime: PerInvocation` on `RustUpgrader` can't express "this upgrader also owns a nested, supervised sub-resource with its own restart lifecycle." C++ needs the same nesting from a different angle: `ClangAstUpgrader{PerCall}` and `ClangdUpgrader{Session}` are two separate trait impls for one language, because a single impl can't honestly carry two lifetimes. An upgrader declares a set of typed sub-resources, each with its own lifetime, rather than being forced into one bucket.
